flagged.title: Medieval Migrants: Hanseatic Merchants, Jews & Lombards
flagged.reason: The video explicitly frames and teaches section 5 around an incorrect '4-mark comparison question' (both voiced and on slides at 01:07, 07:02, and 07:18), whereas the AQA GCSE comparison question is worth 8 marks, leading students to write inadequate 4-mark responses.

mark_affecting.quote: Finally, section five: comparing migrations, acing the four-mark question. You need to ace the four-mark comparison question...

flagged.title: Expansion in India: Company to Crown
flagged.reason: The video presents Oudh as being annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse rather than for alleged misgovernment, a key distinction required by GCSE examiners.

mark_affecting.quote: Take the Doctrine of Lapse, introduced by Lord Dalhousie. From 1848 to 1856, this policy allowed the company to just annex any Indian state whose ruler died without a natural-born male heir... The final straw was the 1856 annexation of Oudh.

flagged.title: The End of Empire: Wars, Suez & Independence
flagged.reason: The video repeats the stale claim that Britain owed the US four years of national income in 1945 (F40), which teaches a grossly inaccurate economic fact that featured in the lesson mark scheme.

mark_affecting.quote: They owed the US four entire years' worth of their national income.

flagged.title: Windrush, Commonwealth Migration & the Legacy of Empire
flagged.reason: The video includes mark-affecting chronological and causal errors regarding the 1948 Nationality Act, Claudia Jones's founding of the West Indian Gazette, and the Windrush scandal facts.

mark_affecting.quote: Passed just three weeks before the Windrush arrived, the 1948 British Nationality Act...
Right after the Notting Hill attacks, she founded the West Indian Gazette...
Back in 2017, the Home Office destroyed the original landing card archives... At least 164 people were illegally removed...

flagged.title: Britain & Europe: From EEC to Brexit
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly claims Polish-born residents were the largest non-UK-born group in the 2011 census (India was first, Poland second) and that immigration was the single most important issue for Leave voters (sovereignty was first at 49%, immigration second at 33%).

mark_affecting.quote: Polish-born residents were the largest non-UK-born group in the entire country.
polling consistently showed that immigration was the single most important issue for Leave voters.
